# KohNoor — full guide text

## Mingora & Saidu Sharif (Swat Valley)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/mingora/
Altitude: about 980 m. From Islamabad: about 250 km, 4–5 h. Best season: All year. Vehicle: Any car. Mobile signal: All networks.

The twin cities at the heart of Swat: Mingora the busy market town, Saidu Sharif the old seat of the Wali of Swat. Every trip into the valley starts here.

History: Saidu Sharif grew around the shrine of the 19th-century saint Akhund of Swat, Abdul Ghafoor. His grandson Miangul Abdul Wadud founded the State of Swat and made Saidu its capital, building the government offices, hospital and school that still stand.

Things to do: Swat Museum and the Butkara stupa (both a few minutes away); Mingora bazaar for Swati shawls, honey and dried fruit; Fizagat Park on the riverbank in the evening; Saidu Sharif's old state buildings and the Wali's mosque.

Getting there: From Islamabad take the M-1 motorway and turn onto the Swat Expressway at Kernal Sher Khan interchange. Daewoo and other coaches run from Islamabad and Rawalpindi.

Stay: From budget hotels in the bazaar to mid-range and upscale hotels along the river and in Saidu Sharif. Food: Chapli kabab, river trout, Swati rice and local honey.

Tips: Last city with full banking: withdraw cash for the upper valley here. Traffic in Mingora is heavy at midday; leave early for Kalam.

## Swat Museum (Swat Valley)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/swat-museum/
Altitude: about 980 m. From Islamabad: about 250 km, 4–5 h. Best season: All year. Vehicle: Any car. Mobile signal: All networks.

A small, excellent museum on the Mingora–Saidu road holding Gandhara sculpture from the valley's Buddhist sites: Buddhas, scenes from the Buddha's life, jewellery and coins.

History: Much of its collection came from excavations by the Italian Archaeological Mission, which has worked in Swat since 1955. The building was damaged in the 2005 earthquake and during the conflict years, and was rebuilt and reopened with Japanese and Italian help.

Things to do: Gandhara stone reliefs telling the Buddha's life story; Finds from Butkara and Udegram; Ethnographic hall with Swati woodwork and embroidery.

Getting there: On the main road between Mingora and Saidu Sharif.

Stay: Stay in Mingora. Food: Cafés in Saidu Sharif.

Tips: Check the opening days before you go; government museums usually close one day a week. Combine with Butkara stupa in one morning.

## Butkara Stupa (Swat Valley)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/butkara/
Altitude: about 980 m. From Islamabad: about 252 km, 4–5 h. Best season: All year. Vehicle: Any car. Mobile signal: All networks.

The ruins of one of the most important Buddhist sanctuaries of Gandhara, right inside Mingora: a great central stupa ringed by more than two hundred smaller stupas and shrines.

History: The first stupa here is believed to date to the time of the Mauryan emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BC. It was enlarged again and again over a thousand years. Italian archaeologists excavated it from 1956, and many of its carvings are now in the Swat Museum.

Things to do: Walk the circuit around the main stupa; See how each rebuild encased the older stupa inside.

Getting there: Short drive or rickshaw from Mingora's Gulkada area.

Stay: Stay in Mingora. Food: Mingora bazaar.

Tips: Go in the morning; there is little shade at midday in summer.

## Udegram (Swat Valley)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/udegram/
Altitude: about 1000 m. From Islamabad: about 240 km, 4 h. Best season: Oct–Apr best (cooler). Vehicle: Any car to the village. Mobile signal: All networks.

A village south of Mingora with two layers of history on one hillside: the ruins of the fortress of Raja Gira and the Ghaznavid mosque below it.

History: Udegram is linked with Ora, one of the towns Alexander the Great besieged in 327 BC. On the hill stand the remains of the castle of Raja Gira, the last Hindu ruler of the area. The mosque at its foot, built by the Ghaznavids around 1048, was found by Italian archaeologists in 1985 and is among the oldest mosques in northern Pakistan.

Things to do: Ghaznavid mosque (easy walk); Climb to Raja Gira's castle for valley views (steep, about 45 minutes); Shrine of Pir Khushal Baba nearby.

Getting there: About 7 km from Mingora on the road towards Barikot.

Stay: Stay in Mingora. Food: Bring water for the climb.

Tips: Wear proper shoes for the castle climb. Avoid summer afternoons; the hillside gets very hot.

## Jahanabad Buddha (Swat Valley)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/jahanabad-buddha/
Altitude: about 1100 m. From Islamabad: about 262 km, 4.5 h. Best season: All year. Vehicle: Car to the village, then a short walk. Mobile signal: Most networks.

A giant seated Buddha carved into a granite cliff above the village of Jahanabad (Shakhorai), one of the largest rock carvings of its kind in South Asia.

History: The figure is thought to date to around the 7th century. In 2007 militants drilled and blasted its face. Italian conservators led by the Italian Archaeological Mission restored it in 2016, using careful 3D work rather than inventing a new face.

Things to do: Short walk up through fields to the carving; Combine with Malam Jabba on the same road.

Getting there: North of Manglawar, on the way towards Malam Jabba.

Stay: Mingora or Malam Jabba. Food: Small shops in Manglawar.

Tips: Respect the site: do not climb on the carving.

## Marghazar & White Palace (Swat Valley)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/marghazar/
Altitude: about 1300 m. From Islamabad: about 258 km, 4.5 h. Best season: Mar–Nov. Vehicle: Any car. Mobile signal: Most networks.

A cool side valley 13 km from Saidu Sharif with the white marble summer palace of the first Wali of Swat, now a hotel, at the foot of Elum mountain.

History: Miangul Abdul Wadud built the White Palace as his summer retreat in the 1940s, with marble brought from Rajasthan. Queen Elizabeth II visited Swat in 1961, and local accounts say she stayed here. Mount Elum above it is sacred in local Hindu and Buddhist tradition.

Things to do: Tea on the White Palace lawns; Stream-side walks and picnic spots; Hike towards Elum (full day, take a guide).

Getting there: Road from Saidu Sharif past the Wali's old residence.

Stay: White Palace hotel or day trip from Mingora. Food: Hotel restaurant and dhabas by the stream.

Tips: Weekends get busy with local families; go on a weekday.

## Malam Jabba (Swat Valley)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/malam-jabba/
Altitude: about 2700 m. From Islamabad: about 290 km, 5–6 h. Best season: Snow: Dec–Feb · Green: May–Sep. Vehicle: Car in summer; 4x4 or chains after snowfall. Mobile signal: Jazz, Zong, Telenor.

Pakistan's best-known ski resort, on a ridge about 45 km from Mingora, with ski slopes, a chairlift, zipline and pine forest views in summer.

History: The resort was developed in the 1980s. It was burned down by militants in 2008 and rebuilt and reopened by a private operator in the 2010s. An old Buddhist stupa and monastery stand on the road below the resort.

Things to do: Skiing and snow play in winter; Chairlift and zipline; Forest walks in summer.

Getting there: Mingora → Manglawar → Malam Jabba road (steep, many bends).

Stay: Resort hotel at the top, or guesthouses lower down. Food: Resort restaurant; carry snacks.

Tips: After heavy snow the road may need chains or 4x4; ask in Manglawar. Temperatures drop well below freezing in winter nights.

## Madyan (Swat Valley)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/madyan/
Altitude: about 1320 m. From Islamabad: about 300 km, 5.5 h. Best season: Mar–Nov. Vehicle: Any car. Mobile signal: All networks.

A riverside town where Swat starts to turn into the mountains: cool air, trout and a quieter base than Mingora.

History: Madyan was long a stop on the route up the valley and is known for its traditional Swati woodwork and handmade shawls.

Things to do: Trout lunch by the Swat River; Shawl and handicraft shops; Short drive up to Bishigram valley.

Getting there: On the main road, about 1 hour after Mingora.

Stay: Riverside hotels and guesthouses. Food: Fresh river trout.

Tips: Good night stop if you reach Swat late.

## Bahrain (Swat Valley)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/bahrain/
Altitude: about 1400 m. From Islamabad: about 310 km, 6 h. Best season: Mar–Nov. Vehicle: Any car. Mobile signal: All networks.

A lively town where the Daral stream meets the Swat River, with hotels on the water and the trail to Daral Lake.

History: Its name, meaning two rivers, comes from the meeting of the Daral and the Swat. It is the main town of the Torwali people, who speak their own Dardic language, Torwali.

Things to do: River-view hotels and bazaar; Trek to Daral Lake (see Hidden places).

Getting there: Main Kalam road, about 1.5 hours after Mingora.

Stay: Many hotels along the river. Food: Trout, tikka and bazaar food.

Tips: Last good ATM stop before Kalam; carry enough cash.

## Kalam (Swat Valley)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/kalam/
Altitude: about 2000 m. From Islamabad: about 350 km, 7–8 h. Best season: May–Oct · snow Dec–Feb. Vehicle: Car to Kalam; jeep beyond. Mobile signal: Jazz, Zong, Telenor in town.

The capital of upper Swat, where the Ushu and Utror rivers join to form the Swat River. Pine forests, snow peaks and the base for Mahodand, Ushu and Utror.

History: Kalam is home to the Gawri (Kalami) people, who speak a Dardic language of their own. Before tourism it was a remote valley of wooden villages and terraced fields; the old carved-wood mosques of upper Swat are among its treasures.

Things to do: Ushu Forest and Matiltan (with view of Falak Sar); Day trip by jeep to Mahodand Lake; Utror and Gabral valleys; Kalam bazaar in the evening.

Getting there: Mingora → Madyan → Bahrain → Kalam. The road has improved but some stretches still get damaged by floods and landslides.

Stay: Large choice of hotels; book ahead in June–August and on Eid. Food: Trout, dum pukht, tea houses on the river.

Tips: Bring cash from Mingora; card payment is rare. Hire jeeps from the stand in Kalam bazaar for Mahodand and Ushu; agree the price first. Nights are cold even in July: bring a warm layer.

## Ushu Forest & Matiltan (Swat Valley)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/ushu-matiltan/
Altitude: about 2300 m. From Islamabad: about 360 km, 8 h. Best season: May–Oct. Vehicle: Jeep recommended. Mobile signal: Patchy.

Tall deodar forest just above Kalam leading to Matiltan, where the white wall of Falak Sar (≈ 5,900 m) fills the end of the valley.

History: The forest is part of the old woodland that once covered much of upper Swat; local communities have long managed grazing and wood cutting here.

Things to do: Forest walks and picnics; Matiltan for views of Falak Sar; Continue to Mahodand Lake.

Getting there: Road from Kalam towards Mahodand, 20–40 minutes by jeep.

Stay: Camps and a few hotels; most stay in Kalam. Food: Tea stalls; carry water.

Tips: Do not leave litter in the forest; there is no collection.

## Mahodand Lake (Swat Valley)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/mahodand/
Altitude: about 2865 m. From Islamabad: about 390 km, 9–10 h. Best season: Jun–Sep. Vehicle: 4x4 jeep only. Mobile signal: No signal.

A wide lake about 35–40 km above Kalam surrounded by meadows and snow peaks. Its name means lake of fish, and it is famous for trout.

History: Gujjar herders bring their animals to the meadows around the lake every summer, as they have for generations.

Things to do: Boating and trout fishing; Walk upstream along the meadows; Camping (take a guide).

Getting there: By jeep from Kalam via Ushu and Matiltan; rough track with river crossings, 2–3 hours.

Stay: Seasonal camps; most return to Kalam. Food: Seasonal stalls; carry food and water.

Tips: No phone signal: tell someone your plan before leaving Kalam. Snow can close the track until late May or June.

## Utror & Gabral (Swat Valley)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/utror-gabral/
Altitude: about 2300 m. From Islamabad: about 365 km, 8–9 h. Best season: May–Oct. Vehicle: Jeep recommended beyond Utror. Mobile signal: Limited.

The western branch of upper Swat: quieter than Kalam, with wooden villages, the Utror river and green meadows leading on to Gabral.

History: Utror's old wooden mosque with carved pillars is one of the finest surviving examples of Swat Kohistan woodwork.

Things to do: Old wooden mosque of Utror; Gabral meadows; Base for Kandol and Spin Khwar lakes.

Getting there: Road west from Kalam, about 1 hour to Utror.

Stay: Guesthouses and camps. Food: Simple local food.

Tips: Ask locals about road damage after rain.

## Kandol & Spin Khwar Lakes (Swat Valley)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/kandol-lake/
Altitude: about 2900 m. From Islamabad: about 375 km, 9–10 h. Best season: Jun–Sep. Vehicle: Jeep to the trailhead, then hike. Mobile signal: No signal.

Two quiet alpine lakes above Utror. Kandol is a deep blue lake below pine ridges; Spin Khwar, meaning white stream, sits higher among meadows. Far fewer visitors than Mahodand.

History: Used for centuries as summer pastures by herding families from Utror and the surrounding valleys.

Things to do: Hike from the jeep point to Kandol (about 1–2 hours); Continue to Spin Khwar with a local guide.

Getting there: Jeep from Kalam via Utror to the trailhead, then hike.

Stay: Camping only, with a guide. Food: Carry all food and water.

Tips: Less verified: hire a local guide in Utror. Weather changes fast; start early and be down by afternoon.

## Daral Lake (Swat Valley)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/daral-lake/
Altitude: about 3400 m. From Islamabad: about 315 km, 6 + trek h. Best season: Jul–Sep. Vehicle: Car to Bahrain, then trek. Mobile signal: No signal on the trek.

A remote high lake above Bahrain, reached by a multi-day trek up the Daral stream through forest and herders' huts. Only for fit hikers.

History: The Daral valley is the homeland of Torwali herding families, who move up to its pastures each summer.

Things to do: Two to three day trek with camping.

Getting there: Trek starts from Bahrain up the Daral stream.

Stay: Camping only. Food: Carry all supplies.

Tips: Less verified: go only with an experienced local guide. Not suitable for children or first-time hikers.

## Gabin Jabba (Swat Valley)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/gabin-jabba/
Altitude: about 2500 m. From Islamabad: about 280 km, 5–6 h. Best season: May–Oct. Vehicle: Jeep recommended for the last stretch. Mobile signal: Limited.

A wide, quiet meadow in the hills above Matta, west of the main valley. Open grassland, pine edges and camping under clear skies.

History: A traditional summer pasture of the Matta hills, opened to visitors only in recent years.

Things to do: Camping and stargazing; Short meadow walks.

Getting there: Mingora → Matta → jeep track to the meadow.

Stay: Camps run by local operators. Food: Camp meals.

Tips: Less verified: book through a known camp operator. Nights are cold; bring warm clothes.

## Kaghan (Kaghan & Naran)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/kaghan/
Altitude: about 2000 m. From Islamabad: about 245 km, 5–6 h. Best season: Apr–Oct. Vehicle: Any car. Mobile signal: Jazz, Zong, Telenor.

The town that gives the whole valley its name, set along the Kunhar River below Naran. A calmer stop than Naran with riverside hotels.

History: Kaghan was long the main settlement of the valley, on the summer route from the plains to the high pastures.

Things to do: Riverside hotels and walks; Shogran and Siri Paye are a detour from Kiwai on the way.

Getting there: Islamabad → Hazara Motorway → Mansehra → Balakot → Kaghan.

Stay: Hotels on the river. Food: Trout and roadside dhabas.

Tips: Beyond Naran the road is closed by snow in winter.

## Naran & Lake Saif-ul-Malook (Kaghan & Naran)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/naran/
Altitude: about 2400 m. From Islamabad: about 270 km, 6–7 h. Best season: May–Oct. Vehicle: Car to Naran; jeep to the lake. Mobile signal: Jazz, Zong, Telenor in town.

The busiest summer resort of the north, and the base for Lake Saif-ul-Malook, Lulusar Lake and Babusar Pass.

History: Lake Saif-ul-Malook (≈ 3,200 m) is named after the folk tale of Prince Saif-ul-Malook and the fairy princess Badri Jamala, told in the famous poem by Mian Muhammad Bakhsh. Locals say fairies still come to the lake on full-moon nights.

Things to do: Jeep to Lake Saif-ul-Malook; Lulusar Lake, source of the Kunhar; Babusar Top (≈ 4,170 m) in summer; Naran bazaar.

Getting there: Kaghan → Naran on the main valley road.

Stay: Hundreds of hotels; very busy June–August. Food: Trout, BBQ, pakoras in the bazaar.

Tips: Naran is mostly shut from about November to April. Agree jeep prices for the lake before setting out.

## Chilas (Gilgit-Baltistan)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/chilas/
Altitude: about 1265 m. From Islamabad: about 400 km, 9–10 (via Babusar, summer) h. Best season: Mar–May, Sep–Nov (summer is very hot). Vehicle: Any car on the KKH. Mobile signal: SCOM, Jazz, Zong.

A hot, rocky town on the Indus and the Karakoram Highway, where the Babusar road comes down. Main stop between Kaghan and Gilgit.

History: The rocks along the Indus around Chilas carry tens of thousands of ancient carvings and inscriptions, left by travellers, traders and Buddhist pilgrims over two thousand years. They are among the largest rock-art collections in the world.

Things to do: Rock carvings along the KKH; Views of Nanga Parbat on the way to Raikot Bridge.

Getting there: Summer: Naran → Babusar Top → Chilas. All year: KKH via Besham and Dasu.

Stay: Hotels in Chilas town. Food: Local hotels on the KKH.

Tips: In summer temperatures can pass 40°C; travel early. Babusar Pass is usually open only from about June to October.

## Fairy Meadows (Gilgit-Baltistan)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/fairy-meadows/
Altitude: about 3300 m. From Islamabad: about 470 km, 11–12 + trek h. Best season: May–Oct. Vehicle: Jeep from Raikot Bridge, then 2–3 hour hike. Mobile signal: Weak or none.

A meadow in pine forest facing the north face of Nanga Parbat (8,126 m), the ninth-highest mountain on earth.

History: The German climber Hermann Buhl made the first ascent of Nanga Parbat in 1953. The meadow got its name from German climbers who called it a fairy-tale meadow.

Things to do: Sunrise on Nanga Parbat; Hike to Beyal Camp and the Nanga Parbat viewpoint.

Getting there: KKH to Raikot Bridge → jeep on a narrow cliff track to Tato/Jhel → hike.

Stay: Wooden huts and camps run by locals. Food: Simple camp meals.

Tips: The jeep track is narrow and frightening for some; only use the official jeep stand. Carry warm clothes; nights are near freezing.

## Hunza (Karimabad) (Gilgit-Baltistan)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/hunza/
Altitude: about 2400 m. From Islamabad: about 600 km, 13–15 h. Best season: Apr (blossom) – Oct (autumn colours). Vehicle: Any car on the KKH. Mobile signal: SCOM, Jazz, Zong.

Terraced valley under Rakaposhi and Ultar peaks, with old forts, apricot orchards, Attabad Lake and the road to Khunjerab Pass.

History: Hunza was a kingdom ruled by its Mirs for centuries until 1974. Altit Fort is around 900 years old and Baltit Fort around 700; both were restored by the Aga Khan Trust for Culture. Attabad Lake was formed in 2010 when a huge landslide blocked the Hunza River.

Things to do: Baltit and Altit forts; Eagle's Nest viewpoint; Attabad Lake and Passu Cones; Khunjerab Pass (≈ 4,690 m) on the China border.

Getting there: Islamabad → KKH (or via Babusar in summer) → Gilgit → Hunza. Flights to Gilgit then road.

Stay: Wide choice in Karimabad and Aliabad. Food: Chapshuro, diram fitti, apricot dishes, walnut cake.

Tips: Khunjerab Pass usually closes for winter around December. Gilgit flights are often cancelled for weather; keep a spare day.

## Skardu (Gilgit-Baltistan)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/skardu/
Altitude: about 2230 m. From Islamabad: about 640 km, 18–20 by road h. Best season: Apr–Oct. Vehicle: Car to Skardu; jeep for Deosai and Shigar side valleys. Mobile signal: SCOM, Jazz, Zong.

Capital of Baltistan on the Indus: cold desert, blue lakes and the gateway to K2 and the Baltoro glacier.

History: Baltistan was once called Little Tibet. Kharpocho Fort above Skardu was built by the great Maqpon ruler Ali Sher Khan Anchan in the 16th century. Nearby Shigar Fort, about 400 years old, has been restored and is now a heritage hotel.

Things to do: Upper Kachura and Shangrila lakes; Shigar Fort and valley; Cold desert at Katpana; Deosai Plains (Jul–Sep); Kharpocho Fort.

Getting there: Fly Islamabad–Skardu (weather permitting), or road via KKH and the Skardu road along the Indus.

Stay: From guesthouses to resorts at Shangrila and Shigar. Food: Balti dishes: mamtu, gyal, apricot soup.

Tips: Deosai is snowbound outside summer. Flights are cheap to cancel for weather; keep a buffer day.

## Chitral & Kalash Valleys (Chitral)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/chitral/
Altitude: about 1500 m. From Islamabad: about 365 km, 8–10 h. Best season: May–Oct (Kalash festivals: Chilam Joshi in May). Vehicle: Car to Chitral; jeep useful for Kalash. Mobile signal: Jazz, Zong, Telenor in town.

A remote town under Tirich Mir (7,708 m), the highest peak of the Hindu Kush, and the gateway to the Kalash valleys of Bumburet, Rumbur and Birir.

History: Chitral was ruled by the Mehtars until 1969. Chitral Fort and the Shahi Mosque (1924) stand on the riverbank. The Kalash people keep their own faith, language and festivals, unlike any other culture in Pakistan.

Things to do: Shahi Mosque and Chitral Fort; Kalash valleys (Bumburet is easiest); Garam Chashma hot springs; Shandur Pass polo festival (usually July).

Getting there: Islamabad → Swat Expressway → Dir → Lowari Tunnel → Chitral. Also flights.

Stay: Hotels in Chitral; guesthouses in Bumburet. Food: Chitrali bread, walnuts, local cheese.

Tips: Ask permission before photographing Kalash people, especially women. Foreign visitors may need to register with police.

## Rawalakot & Banjosa (Azad Kashmir)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/rawalakot/
Altitude: about 1615 m. From Islamabad: about 120 km, 3–4 h. Best season: All year (snow Dec–Feb). Vehicle: Any car. Mobile signal: SCOM, Zong, Jazz.

Main town of Poonch district in green pine hills, with Banjosa Lake and Toli Pir close by. The easiest mountain trip from Islamabad.

History: Poonch has a proud military tradition and was a centre of the 1947 movement that formed Azad Kashmir. Sardar Muhammad Ibrahim Khan, first president of Azad Kashmir, came from this area.

Things to do: Banjosa Lake (about 20 km); Toli Pir meadow and viewpoint; Rawalakot bazaar.

Getting there: Islamabad → Kohala or Azad Pattan → Rawalakot.

Stay: Hotels in Rawalakot and at Banjosa. Food: Local Pahari dishes and kebabs.

Tips: Good choice for a two-day family trip.

## Neelum Valley (Azad Kashmir)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/neelum/
Altitude: about 2000 m. From Islamabad: about 270 km, 7–9 to Sharda h. Best season: Apr–Oct. Vehicle: Car to Sharda/Kel; jeep beyond. Mobile signal: SCOM, Zong; patchy.

A 200 km valley along the Neelum River from Muzaffarabad: Keran, Sharda, Kel, Arang Kel and Taobat, with Ratti Gali Lake high above Dowarian.

History: Sharda holds the ruins of Sharda Peeth, once a famous centre of learning that gave its name to the old Sharda script. Parts of the valley road run beside the Line of Control.

Things to do: Keran riverside; Sharda ruins; Arang Kel village (cable car and hike from Kel); Ratti Gali Lake by jeep from Dowarian (summer).

Getting there: Islamabad → Muzaffarabad → Neelum road.

Stay: Hotels and guesthouses in Keran, Sharda and Kel. Food: Trout and local food.

Tips: Respect restrictions near the Line of Control and carry your CNIC. Do not photograph security posts.

## Murree (Murree & Galiyat)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/murree/
Altitude: about 2290 m. From Islamabad: about 60 km, 1.5–2 h. Best season: All year · snow Dec–Feb. Vehicle: Any car (chains in heavy snow). Mobile signal: All networks.

Pakistan's best-known hill station, an hour and a half from Islamabad, with Mall Road, pine ridges and winter snow.

History: The British founded Murree in 1851 as a sanatorium and summer headquarters for the Punjab government. Its churches, Mall Road and old hotels date from that time.

Things to do: Mall Road walk and Kashmir Point; Patriata (New Murree) chairlift and cable car; Pindi Point views; Snowfall in winter.

Getting there: Islamabad → Murree Expressway, about 1.5 hours without traffic.

Stay: Hundreds of hotels from budget to upscale; book ahead on weekends. Food: Mall Road cafés, corn on the cob, tea and pakoras.

Tips: In heavy snowfall, follow police advisories; in January 2022 people died stuck in their cars in a snowstorm. Weekends and public holidays bring huge traffic jams; go on weekdays.

## Nathia Gali & Ayubia (Murree & Galiyat)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/nathia-gali/
Altitude: about 2500 m. From Islamabad: about 85 km, 2.5 h. Best season: All year · snow Dec–Feb. Vehicle: Any car (chains in heavy snow). Mobile signal: All networks.

The quieter, greener hill stations of the Galiyat ridge between Murree and Abbottabad: oak and pine forest, Mukshpuri and Miranjani peaks and the Pipeline walking track.

History: Nathia Gali was the summer headquarters of the British governor of the North-West Frontier Province. The old Governor House and St Matthew's Church still stand. Ayubia was named after President Ayub Khan.

Things to do: Pipeline Track from Dunga Gali to Ayubia (about 4 km, flat); Mukshpuri or Miranjani hike; Ayubia chairlift; Bird watching in the forest.

Getting there: Islamabad → Murree → Galiyat road, or from Abbottabad.

Stay: Hotels and cottages in Nathia Gali, Dunga Gali and Bhurban. Food: Hotel restaurants and roadside tea stalls.

Tips: Leopards live in these forests; do not walk trails alone after dark.

## Kumrat Valley (Dir & Kumrat)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/kumrat/
Altitude: about 2300 m. From Islamabad: about 400 km, 9–10 h. Best season: Jun–Sep. Vehicle: Car to Thall; jeep into the valley. Mobile signal: Weak or none beyond Thall.

A deep valley of giant deodar trees, meadows and the Panjkora River in Upper Dir. It became famous after 2016 and is now one of the most loved camping spots in the north.

History: The valley is home to Kohistani communities whose carved wooden mosques, such as the old mosque at Thall, are among the finest in the region.

Things to do: Kumrat forest and riverside camping; Jahaz Banda meadow (hike or jeep + hike); Kala Chashma springs; Thall's old wooden mosque.

Getting there: Islamabad → Swat Expressway → Chakdara → Dir → Thall → jeep to Kumrat.

Stay: Camps and simple huts; a few hotels in Thall. Food: Camp meals and trout.

Tips: Bring cash from Dir; there are no ATMs in the valley. Rivers are fast and cold: do not swim.

## Shogran & Siri Paye (Kaghan & Naran)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/shogran/
Altitude: about 2360 m. From Islamabad: about 210 km, 5 h. Best season: Apr–Oct · snow Dec–Feb. Vehicle: Car to Kiwai; jeep up to Shogran and Siri Paye. Mobile signal: Jazz, Zong.

A forested plateau above Kiwai with views of Malika Parbat, and the open meadows of Siri Paye a short jeep ride higher. A gentler alternative to Naran.

History: Shogran was a summer grazing ground before hotels arrived in the 1990s. Siri and Paye are two meadows, named after the small lake (siri) and the grazing ground (paye).

Things to do: Jeep to Siri Paye meadows; Short walks in the pine forest; Views of Malika Parbat and Makra peak.

Getting there: Balakot → Kiwai → steep road to Shogran.

Stay: Hotels and cottages in Shogran. Food: Hotel restaurants.

Tips: The Kiwai–Shogran road is steep; low-power cars struggle.

## Babusar Top & Lulusar (Kaghan & Naran)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/babusar/
Altitude: about 4170 m. From Islamabad: about 340 km, 8 h. Best season: Jun–Sep (pass usually open Jun–Oct). Vehicle: Car in summer if driven carefully. Mobile signal: Weak.

The highest point of the Kaghan Valley road, a windswept pass between Kaghan and Chilas, with Lulusar Lake on the way up. On clear days Nanga Parbat shows on the horizon.

History: Babusar has been a route between the Kaghan Valley and the Indus for centuries. The paved road made it a summer shortcut from Islamabad to Gilgit-Baltistan.

Things to do: Lulusar Lake, source of the Kunhar River; Photo stop at the top; Continue down to Chilas.

Getting there: Naran → Batakundi → Lulusar → Babusar Top.

Stay: Stay in Naran or Chilas. Food: Tea stalls at the top in summer.

Tips: Altitude above 4,000 m: do not run or stay long if you feel dizzy. Snow can close the pass any day outside summer.

## Gilgit City (Gilgit-Baltistan)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/gilgit/
Altitude: about 1500 m. From Islamabad: about 500 km, 11–14 h. Best season: Mar–Nov. Vehicle: Any car. Mobile signal: SCOM, Jazz, Zong.

The capital and crossroads of Gilgit-Baltistan, on the Gilgit River, where roads branch to Hunza, Naltar, Ghizer and Skardu.

History: Gilgit was an old Silk Road stop and later the base of the British Gilgit Agency. On 1 November 1947 local forces rose against Dogra rule, and the region joined Pakistan; 1 November is still celebrated as Independence Day of Gilgit-Baltistan.

Things to do: Kargah Buddha rock carving (about 7th century); Gilgit bazaar for gems and dried fruit; Polo ground matches.

Getting there: Summer: via Babusar. All year: Karakoram Highway. Flights from Islamabad.

Stay: Wide choice of hotels. Food: Chapshuro, local trout, dried apricots.

Tips: Good place to rest one night before going higher.

## Naltar Valley (Gilgit-Baltistan)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/naltar/
Altitude: about 2900 m. From Islamabad: about 540 km, 13–15 h. Best season: Jun–Sep · skiing Dec–Feb. Vehicle: Jeep from Nomal. Mobile signal: Limited.

A pine valley north of Gilgit with colourful lakes: Satrangi (seven-colour) Lake, Blue Lake and Pari Lake. In winter it hosts skiing.

History: The Pakistan Air Force has run a ski resort here for decades, and Naltar has hosted national and international ski events.

Things to do: Satrangi, Blue and Pari lakes; Forest walks; Skiing in winter.

Getting there: Gilgit → Nomal → jeep track to Naltar Bala.

Stay: Guesthouses and camps. Food: Simple local food.

Tips: The jeep track is rough; take an experienced local driver.

## Attabad Lake (Gilgit-Baltistan)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/attabad/
Altitude: about 2550 m. From Islamabad: about 620 km, 14–16 h. Best season: All year (frozen edges in winter). Vehicle: Any car on the KKH. Mobile signal: SCOM, Jazz, Zong.

A turquoise lake along the Karakoram Highway between Hunza and Gojal, with boating, jet skis and lakeside resorts.

History: In January 2010 a huge landslide at Attabad village blocked the Hunza River, killing 20 people and drowning villages and part of the highway. The lake that formed is now one of Pakistan's most photographed sights. Tunnels built with Chinese help reopened the road in 2015.

Things to do: Boat ride on the lake; Drive through the Attabad tunnels; Lakeside cafés and resorts.

Getting there: Karimabad → KKH north, about 30 minutes.

Stay: Lakeside resorts or stay in Hunza. Food: Lakeside cafés.

Tips: Wear life jackets on every boat ride.

## Passu & Khunjerab Pass (Gilgit-Baltistan)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/passu-khunjerab/
Altitude: about 2500 m. From Islamabad: about 660 km, 16–18 h. Best season: May–Oct (Khunjerab usually closes for winter). Vehicle: Any car on the KKH. Mobile signal: SCOM; none near the pass.

Upper Hunza (Gojal): the sharp Passu Cones, Hussaini suspension bridge, Passu glacier, and Khunjerab Pass at about 4,690 m on the China border, one of the highest paved border crossings in the world.

History: The Wakhi people of Gojal came here from the Wakhan corridor. Khunjerab means blood valley, an echo of the raids on old caravans. The Karakoram Highway crossing opened to travellers in the 1980s.

Things to do: Passu Cones viewpoint; Hussaini suspension bridge; Borith Lake; Khunjerab Pass and national park (snow leopard, ibex, marmots).

Getting there: Hunza → KKH north through Attabad tunnels → Passu → Sost → Khunjerab.

Stay: Guesthouses in Passu, Gulmit and Sost. Food: Wakhi bread and soups.

Tips: Khunjerab is above 4,600 m: stay less than an hour and go back down. Carry your CNIC for checkposts.

## Deosai Plains (Gilgit-Baltistan)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/deosai/
Altitude: about 4100 m. From Islamabad: about 670 km, Skardu + 3 h. Best season: Jul–Sep (snowbound the rest of the year). Vehicle: 4x4 jeep. Mobile signal: No signal.

One of the highest plateaus in the world, a national park of wildflowers and streams, home of the Himalayan brown bear. Sheosar Lake lies at its western edge.

History: Deosai means land of giants in local legend. It became a national park in 1993 to protect its brown bears, whose numbers have grown since.

Things to do: Sheosar Lake; Bara Pani river camp; Watching brown bears and marmots from a distance.

Getting there: Skardu → Sadpara Lake → Deosai by jeep. Can continue to Astore.

Stay: Licensed camps only. Food: Carry food and water.

Tips: Very cold even in summer nights; take a sleeping bag. Never approach or feed bears.

## Shigar Valley (Gilgit-Baltistan)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/shigar/
Altitude: about 2300 m. From Islamabad: about 670 km, Skardu + 1 h. Best season: Apr–Oct. Vehicle: Any car. Mobile signal: SCOM, Zong.

Green valley north of Skardu on the road to K2, with the restored Shigar Fort, the Sarfaranga cold desert and old wooden mosques.

History: Shigar Fort (Fong Khar) was the palace of the Amacha rulers and is around 400 years old. The Aga Khan Trust for Culture restored it and it now operates as a heritage hotel and museum.

Things to do: Shigar Fort and museum; Sarfaranga cold desert; Amburik mosque, one of the oldest in Baltistan.

Getting there: Skardu → Shigar road, about 1 hour.

Stay: Shigar Fort hotel or guesthouses. Food: Balti dishes.

Tips: Base for the long trek to K2 base camp (needs permits and a licensed operator).

## Khaplu (Gilgit-Baltistan)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/khaplu/
Altitude: about 2600 m. From Islamabad: about 740 km, Skardu + 3 h. Best season: Apr–Oct. Vehicle: Any car. Mobile signal: SCOM, Zong.

Quiet town in the Ghanche valley east of Skardu, with the beautiful Khaplu Palace and Chaqchan Mosque, and views towards Masherbrum.

History: Khaplu Palace was built in the 19th century by the Yabgo rajas of Khaplu and restored by the Aga Khan Trust. Chaqchan Mosque is believed to date to the 14th century, linked with the preacher Mir Syed Ali Hamdani.

Things to do: Khaplu Palace; Chaqchan Mosque; Drive on towards Machulo and Hushe.

Getting there: Skardu → along the Shyok River, about 3 hours.

Stay: Khaplu Palace hotel or guesthouses. Food: Balti food, apricots.

Tips: Good choice for travellers who want Baltistan without crowds.

## Astore & Rama Meadows (Gilgit-Baltistan)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/astore-rama/
Altitude: about 3300 m. From Islamabad: about 470 km, 11–13 h. Best season: Jun–Sep. Vehicle: Car to Astore; jeep to Rama. Mobile signal: SCOM in Astore.

Valley on the east side of Nanga Parbat. Above Astore town, Rama meadows and Rama Lake sit under the Nanga Parbat massif.

History: Astore lay on the old route from Kashmir to Gilgit via the Burzil Pass. Its villages still keep traditions of the Shina-speaking people.

Things to do: Rama meadows and forest; Rama Lake (hike); Rupal valley and Nanga Parbat south face.

Getting there: KKH → Jaglot → Astore → jeep to Rama.

Stay: Guesthouses and camps. Food: Simple local food.

Tips: Combine with Deosai: the road crosses from Astore to Skardu in summer.

## Phander & Ghizer (Gilgit-Baltistan)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/phander/
Altitude: about 2900 m. From Islamabad: about 680 km, Gilgit + 5–6 h. Best season: May–Oct (autumn colours Oct). Vehicle: Car if driven carefully; jeep better. Mobile signal: SCOM.

The western valleys of Gilgit-Baltistan: Phander Lake, trout streams and willow trees that turn gold in October, on the road towards Shandur.

History: Ghizer lies on the old route between Gilgit and Chitral over the Shandur Pass, where the famous polo match between Gilgit and Chitral is played each summer.

Things to do: Phander Lake; Khalti Lake trout; Drive on to Shandur Pass in summer.

Getting there: Gilgit → Gahkuch → Gupis → Phander.

Stay: Guesthouses and small hotels. Food: Trout.

Tips: October autumn colours are spectacular but nights are freezing.

## Kalash Valleys (Chitral)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/kalash/
Altitude: about 2000 m. From Islamabad: about 405 km, 9–11 h. Best season: May–Oct · festivals: Chilam Joshi (May), Uchal (Aug), Chaumos (Dec). Vehicle: Car to Bumburet if driven carefully; jeep for Rumbur and Birir. Mobile signal: Limited.

Three valleys near Chitral, Bumburet, Rumbur and Birir, home to the Kalash people, with their own faith, colourful dress, wooden houses and spring, summer and winter festivals.

History: The Kalash are one of the smallest communities of Pakistan, with a language (Kalasha) and religion unlike their neighbours'. Their festivals mark the seasons, and their culture is a protected heritage.

Things to do: Kalash museum (Kalasha Dur) in Bumburet; Village walks with a local guide; Festivals if your dates match.

Getting there: Chitral → Ayun → Bumburet road (narrow).

Stay: Guesthouses run by Kalash families. Food: Local walnut bread, cheese, grape juice.

Tips: Always ask before photographing anyone. Do not enter graveyards or sacred places.

## Muzaffarabad & Pir Chinasi (Azad Kashmir)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/muzaffarabad/
Altitude: about 740 m. From Islamabad: about 140 km, 3–4 h. Best season: All year. Vehicle: Any car. Mobile signal: All networks.

Capital of Azad Kashmir where the Neelum and Jhelum rivers meet. Pir Chinasi, about 30 km away at around 2,900 m, gives wide views over the valley.

History: Founded by Sultan Muzaffar Khan in the 17th century, whose Red Fort still stands by the river. The city was largely destroyed in the October 2005 earthquake and rebuilt.

Things to do: Red Fort; Domel, where the Neelum meets the Jhelum; Pir Chinasi shrine and viewpoint.

Getting there: Islamabad → Murree → Kohala → Muzaffarabad.

Stay: Hotels in the city. Food: Kashmiri food.

Tips: Gateway to Neelum Valley: fill up and withdraw cash here.

## Arang Kel (Azad Kashmir)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/arang-kel/
Altitude: about 2400 m. From Islamabad: about 300 km, 9–10 h. Best season: May–Oct. Vehicle: Car to Kel, then cable car or a steep hike. Mobile signal: SCOM, weak.

A storybook village of wooden houses on a high meadow above Kel in upper Neelum, reached by a small cable car across the river and a steep walk.

History: Arang Kel stayed almost unknown until the 2000s; its isolation kept its wooden village and fields intact.

Things to do: Cable car from Kel; Meadow walk to the village; Sunset over Neelum.

Getting there: Muzaffarabad → Neelum road → Kel → cable car.

Stay: Guesthouses in Arang Kel and Kel. Food: Simple local food.

Tips: The hike is steep: good shoes and water.

## Ratti Gali Lake (Azad Kashmir)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/ratti-gali/
Altitude: about 3700 m. From Islamabad: about 240 km, 7 + jeep h. Best season: Jul–Sep. Vehicle: 4x4 jeep from Dowarian, then a short hike. Mobile signal: No signal.

A glacial lake surrounded by flower meadows and snow peaks above Dowarian in Neelum. One of the most beautiful lakes in Kashmir.

History: The meadows around the lake are old summer pastures of Gujjar and Bakarwal herders.

Things to do: Jeep to base camp, hike to the lake; Camping in the meadows.

Getting there: Neelum road → Dowarian → jeep track (2–3 hours) → hike.

Stay: Camps at base camp. Food: Camp meals.

Tips: Snow often blocks the jeep track until July. Start early: weather turns in the afternoon.

## Jahaz Banda (Dir & Kumrat)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/jahaz-banda/
Altitude: about 3100 m. From Islamabad: about 410 km, 10–11 + hike h. Best season: Jun–Sep. Vehicle: Car to Thall; jeep to Jandrai, then 3–4 hour hike. Mobile signal: No signal on the meadow.

A wide, flat alpine meadow above the Kumrat side of Upper Dir, ringed by pine forest and snow ridges. Herders' huts, grazing horses and a sky full of stars at night.

History: For generations Gujjar and Kohistani herding families have brought their cattle up to Jahaz Banda each summer; the stone huts on the meadow are their seasonal homes.

Things to do: Hike up from Jandrai village through the forest; Camp on the meadow and watch the sunrise; Day hike on to Katora Lake; Visit the waterfall on the way up.

Getting there: Drive to Thall via Dir and Sheringal, take a local jeep to Jandrai, then hike or hire a horse up to the meadow.

Stay: Simple camps and huts run by locals on the meadow in season; bring a warm sleeping bag. Food: Basic meals (daal, rice, tea) at the camps; carry snacks and water purification.

Tips: Hire horses or porters in Jandrai if carrying heavy gear. Nights are cold even in July; pack a down jacket.

## Katora Lake (Dir & Kumrat)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/katora-lake/
Altitude: about 3500 m. From Islamabad: about 410 km, 10–11 + 2-day hike h. Best season: Jul–Sep. Vehicle: Jeep to Jandrai, then hike via Jahaz Banda. Mobile signal: No signal.

A bowl-shaped glacial lake (katora means bowl) of icy turquoise water, tucked under snowfields above Jahaz Banda. One of the most striking lakes in Upper Dir.

History: The lake was known mainly to local shepherds until trekkers began posting photos in the 2010s; it is still reached only on foot.

Things to do: Trek from Jahaz Banda (about 3–4 hours each way); Photograph the snow bridge and glacier above the lake.

Getting there: Base yourself at Jahaz Banda, then hike up the valley with a local guide.

Stay: Camp at Jahaz Banda; there is no lodging at the lake. Food: Carry all food and water.

Tips: Snow can cover the trail until early July. Go with a guide from Jandrai; the route is not marked.

## Shandur Pass (Chitral)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/shandur/
Altitude: about 3700 m. From Islamabad: about 530 km, 13–15 h. Best season: Jun–Sep (polo festival in early July). Vehicle: 4x4 or jeep recommended from Mastuj. Mobile signal: Weak or none.

A high, open plateau between Chitral and Ghizer with a lake and the famous polo ground often called the roof of the world.

History: The Shandur Polo Festival, played between the teams of Chitral and Gilgit, is held here every July and draws crowds from across Pakistan.

Things to do: Watch the Shandur Polo Festival in early July; Walk around Shandur Lake; Cross over into Phander and Ghizer.

Getting there: From Chitral drive via Booni and Mastuj up to the pass; or come from Gilgit via Gupis and Phander.

Stay: Tents during the festival; otherwise rest houses in Mastuj or Phander. Food: Food stalls during the festival only; carry supplies at other times.

Tips: Festival dates change each year; check before planning. Altitude is high; go slowly if coming straight from the plains.

## Garam Chashma (Chitral)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/garam-chashma/
Altitude: about 2500 m. From Islamabad: about 410 km, 9–11 h. Best season: Apr–Oct. Vehicle: Any car in dry weather; jeep in winter. Mobile signal: Patchy.

A green valley northwest of Chitral town known for its natural hot springs, used for bathing by locals and visitors.

History: The springs have long been believed to help with joint pain and skin problems, and simple bathhouses grew up around them.

Things to do: Bathe in the hot spring baths; Fish for trout in the Lutkoh River; Drive through the orchards of the Lutkoh valley.

Getting there: Drive about 45 km from Chitral town along the Lutkoh River.

Stay: A few small guesthouses; most visitors stay in Chitral town. Food: Local trout and simple meals.

Tips: Separate bathing times for men and women at some baths. Good half-day trip from Chitral.

## Upper Kachura Lake (Gilgit-Baltistan)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/kachura/
Altitude: about 2500 m. From Islamabad: about 660 km, Flight + 40 min h. Best season: Apr–Oct. Vehicle: Any car to the lake path. Mobile signal: SCOM, Zong.

A clear, deep-green lake surrounded by apricot trees and steep mountains, a short drive from Skardu. Quieter than its famous neighbour Shangrila (Lower Kachura).

History: Shangrila resort was built on the lower lake in the 1980s; the upper lake has stayed largely as it was.

Things to do: Walk down to the lake and take a boat ride; Visit Shangrila resort on the lower lake; Picnic under the apricot trees.

Getting there: About 30 km from Skardu city on the road to Shangrila; a short walk down from the road.

Stay: Hotels in Skardu or resorts around Kachura. Food: Small café at the lake; full meals in Skardu or Shangrila.

Tips: Go early morning for calm water and reflections. Bring cash; card payment is rare.

## Sarfaranga Cold Desert (Gilgit-Baltistan)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/sarfaranga/
Altitude: about 2200 m. From Islamabad: about 650 km, Flight + 30 min h. Best season: Apr–Oct. Vehicle: Jeep or 4x4 for the dunes. Mobile signal: SCOM, Zong.

White sand dunes at high altitude, framed by snow peaks, in the Shigar–Skardu area. A rare cold desert landscape.

History: Locals have long used the dunes as pasture margins; in recent years they became popular for jeep rallies.

Things to do: Jeep ride over the dunes; Sunset photography over the mountains; Visit during the Sarfaranga jeep rally if it is held.

Getting there: A short drive from Skardu towards Shigar; hire a local jeep.

Stay: Hotels in Skardu; camping possible with a guide. Food: Carry water and snacks.

Tips: Afternoon winds can be strong. Go with a local driver who knows the dunes.

## Manthoka Waterfall (Gilgit-Baltistan)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/manthoka/
Altitude: about 2600 m. From Islamabad: about 730 km, Flight + 2.5 hrs h. Best season: Apr–Oct. Vehicle: Any car. Mobile signal: SCOM.

A tall waterfall falling through a green gorge in Kharmang district, south-east of Skardu. Small eateries sit right beside the cold spray.

History: Kharmang lies on the old route along the Indus towards Ladakh; the area opened up to tourism only recently.

Things to do: Lunch at the café beside the falls; Walk up the gorge; Combine with a drive along the Indus in Kharmang.

Getting there: Drive from Skardu along the Indus towards Kharmang, about 2–2.5 hours.

Stay: Day trip from Skardu; a few small guesthouses near the falls. Food: Trout and simple meals at the waterfall cafés.

Tips: Carry your CNIC; there are checkposts. Water is ice cold even in summer.

## Borith Lake & Hussaini (Gilgit-Baltistan)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/borith/
Altitude: about 2600 m. From Islamabad: about 640 km, 15–17 h. Best season: Apr–Oct. Vehicle: Any car on the KKH; short track to the lake. Mobile signal: SCOM.

A small brackish lake above Hussaini village in Upper Hunza (Gojal), with views of the Passu Cones and the Batura glacier.

History: Hussaini village is famous for its suspension bridge over the Hunza River, rebuilt many times by the villagers themselves.

Things to do: Cross the Hussaini suspension bridge (carefully); Walk to Borith Lake; Hike towards Passu Glacier.

Getting there: Drive up the KKH past Attabad Lake to Hussaini, then a short drive or walk up to the lake.

Stay: Borith Lake Hotel and guesthouses in Passu and Gulmit. Food: Hunza food in Gulmit and Passu.

Tips: The bridge sways a lot; avoid it in strong wind. Bird-watching is best in spring and autumn.

## Khalti Lake (Gilgit-Baltistan)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/khalti/
Altitude: about 2200 m. From Islamabad: about 700 km, 16–18 h. Best season: Apr–Oct (frozen in winter). Vehicle: Any car on the Gilgit–Chitral road. Mobile signal: SCOM.

A long, calm, deep-blue lake beside the road in Ghizer, famous for trout and for freezing over completely in winter.

History: The lake formed from a landslide on the Ghizer River; local people now fish here and skate on its ice in winter.

Things to do: Trout fishing (permit needed); Boat ride on the lake; Drive on to Phander.

Getting there: From Gilgit drive west via Gahkuch and Gupis; the lake is just past Gupis.

Stay: PTDC motel and guesthouses at Gupis/Khalti. Food: Fresh trout at the lakeside.

Tips: Get a fishing permit from the fisheries office. In winter the road is open but very cold.

## Dudipatsar Lake (Kaghan & Naran)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/dudipatsar/
Altitude: about 3800 m. From Islamabad: about 315 km, 7–8 + 5–7 hour hike h. Best season: Jul–Sep. Vehicle: Car to Besal, then hike. Mobile signal: No signal.

A high glacial lake inside Lulusar–Dudipatsar National Park, its name meaning white lake for the snow around it. Reached only on foot.

History: The area is protected as a national park for its snow leopards, ibex and alpine flowers.

Things to do: Trek from Besal (one long day each way); Camp near the lake; Look for wildflowers in July and August.

Getting there: Drive from Naran towards Babusar to Besal, then trek up the valley with a guide.

Stay: Camping only; local guides arrange tents. Food: Carry all food.

Tips: Very cold at night; serious camping gear needed. Hire a guide and porters at Besal.

## Sharda (Azad Kashmir)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/sharda/
Altitude: about 1980 m. From Islamabad: about 270 km, 7–9 h. Best season: Apr–Oct. Vehicle: Any car. Mobile signal: SCOM, Zong.

A riverside town in the Neelum Valley with the ruins of the ancient Sharda Peeth temple and university on the hillside above.

History: Sharda Peeth was a renowned centre of learning in the first millennium, and the Sharada script is named after it.

Things to do: Visit the Sharda Peeth ruins; Walk across the suspension bridge; Drive on to Kel and Arang Kel.

Getting there: Drive from Muzaffarabad along the Neelum road via Athmuqam and Kel road.

Stay: Guesthouses and hotels along the river. Food: River trout and simple local food.

Tips: Sharda is near the Line of Control; carry your CNIC. Foreigners may need extra permission for some areas.

## Taobat (Azad Kashmir)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/taobat/
Altitude: about 2300 m. From Islamabad: about 330 km, 10–12 h. Best season: May–Oct. Vehicle: Jeep beyond Kel. Mobile signal: Weak.

The last village at the far end of the Neelum Valley, with wooden houses, meadows and the river running clear and fast.

History: Old villages of wood and stone here still follow the traditional Kashmiri building style.

Things to do: Walk the meadows along the river; Photograph the wooden houses; Visit Halmat on the way.

Getting there: Drive to Kel, then take a jeep along the rough road to Taobat.

Stay: A few basic guesthouses. Food: Simple meals at guesthouses.

Tips: Road can close after rain. Close to the LoC; follow local advice.

## Leepa Valley (Azad Kashmir)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/leepa/
Altitude: about 1900 m. From Islamabad: about 230 km, 7–8 h. Best season: May–Oct (autumn colours in October). Vehicle: Jeep or high car over Reshian pass. Mobile signal: Patchy.

A green valley of rice terraces and wooden houses on the eastern side of AJK, especially beautiful in autumn when the walnut and rice fields turn gold.

History: Leepa has kept its traditional wooden Kashmiri houses and terraced red-rice farming.

Things to do: Walk the rice terraces; See traditional wooden houses; Cross the Reshian pass viewpoints.

Getting there: Drive from Muzaffarabad via Hattian Bala and Reshian over the pass into the valley.

Stay: Guesthouses and a few hotels in the valley. Food: Leepa red rice and local dishes.

Tips: Pass road may close in winter snow. Near the LoC; carry ID.

## Miranjani Peak (Murree & Galiyat)
URL: https://kohnoor.pages.dev/places/miranjani/
Altitude: about 2990 m. From Islamabad: about 90 km, 2.5 + 2–3 hour hike h. Best season: Apr–Nov (snow trek in winter). Vehicle: Any car to Nathia Gali. Mobile signal: Good near the trailhead.

The highest peak of the Galiyat, reached by a forest trail from Nathia Gali. On clear days you can see Nanga Parbat from the top.

History: Hikers have used the trail since the British era, when Nathia Gali was the summer seat of the NWFP government.

Things to do: Hike from Nathia Gali (about 2–3 hours up); Sunrise or clear-day views of Nanga Parbat; Combine with Mushkpuri Top.

Getting there: Start from behind the church in Nathia Gali; the trail is well used.

Stay: Hotels in Nathia Gali. Food: Carry water; food in Nathia Gali.

Tips: Start early; clouds build by afternoon. Snow and ice in winter need proper shoes.
